question.text: Which of the group element does not form M(III) iodide?

solution.text: Due to inert pair effect, <math> <mrow> <mtext>Tl</mtext></mrow> </math> prefers its <math> <mrow> <mtext>+1</mtext></mrow> </math> oxidation state while bonding with iodine and <math> <mrow>  <mtext>TlI</mtext></mrow></math>form. Although thallium <math> <mrow> <mtext>(Tl)</mtext></mrow> </math> form <math><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></math>, but the O.S. of thallium is <math> <mrow> <mtext>+1</mtext></mrow> </math> in this compound, because iodine is present as tri-iodide ion <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msubsup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math>
